column1: # The userspace smoke scenario — what a user would call working, in one place.
# One step per line: the command, a tab, and the line its output must produce. An empty expectation
# means the step has nothing to say and the next prompt is the whole of its evidence — a write.
# Two rules, both of them cause (h) in TEST_GATES.md:
#   * The expectation is matched against a *whole line*. The guest echoes what it is sent, so
#     `# /bin/echo smoke-ok` would satisfy a substring search for `smoke-ok` on a shell that
#     echoed the line and never ran the command. Anchored, only the output can satisfy it.
#   * The expectation is therefore never a prefix or substring of its own command.
# Why these three steps: they are the ones that need the file-backed exec path (an image binary
# exec'd by the shell), the filesystem (a file created, and read back through a second open), and a
# second process — which is what was broken, invisibly, when init stopped at `RTS_PAGEFAULT`
# (finding 57). `boot.cjs` and `page.test.js` assert much more on wasm; this is the part every
# target can be asked, and wasm cannot answer for the other three: it has no page faults, so it
# never runs FDIO or the demand-paged path at all.
